title: Day 1 — Arrival 🛬
description: Transfer to hotel. Drop bags, find the nearest trattoria, walk to Trastevere in the evening.
fun_fact: Rome has more than 280 public fountains — the water is drinkable everywhere.

title: Day 2 — Ancient Rome 🏛️
description: Colosseum, Roman Forum, Palatine Hill in the morning. Gelato break at Giolitti. Trevi Fountain at sunset.
fun_fact: The Forum Romanum was the centre of Roman public life for over 1,000 years — elections, trials, triumphs and commerce all happened here.

title: Day 3 — Vatican & Prati 🎨
description: Vatican Museums early (book in advance!), Sistine Chapel, St Peter's. Lunch in Prati neighbourhood.
fun_fact: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling lying on his back over 4 years. He was a sculptor, not a painter — he considered the commission an insult.

title: Day 4 — Borghese & Piazzas 🌿
description: Borghese Gallery (pre-book — only 360 people allowed at a time). Stroll Piazza del Popolo, Spanish Steps, Via Condotti window shopping.
fun_fact: The Borghese Gallery houses one of the finest private art collections ever assembled. Cardinal Borghese spent decades 'acquiring' pieces — some by threatening artists with arrest.

title: Day 5 — Pantheon & Campo de' Fiori ☀️
description: Pantheon in the morning (free, but arrive early). Piazza Navona for coffee. Campo de' Fiori market. Aperitivo somewhere good.
fun_fact: The Pantheon's concrete dome has stood for 1,900 years with no internal supports. The oculus at the top is 9 metres wide — when it rains, the floor drains it.

title: Day 6 — Tivoli Day Trip 🏰
description: 45 minutes from Rome: Villa d'Este with its 500 fountains and terraced gardens, then Hadrian's Villa — the emperor's personal city spanning 120 hectares.
fun_fact: Hadrian's Villa was so vast it had its own baths, libraries, theatres and temples. Hadrian built miniature replicas of his favourite places from across the empire.

title: Day 7 — Last Day in Rome 🍷
description: Slow morning. Testaccio market for lunch — the most authentic food neighbourhood in Rome. Aventine Hill and the Knights of Malta keyhole with a perfect view of St Peter's dome.
fun_fact: Through the keyhole at the Priory of the Knights of Malta on Aventine Hill, you see three countries simultaneously: Italy, Vatican City, and the sovereign territory of the Knights of Malta.

title: Day 8 — Il Monastero Collection 🕌
description: Drive north from Rome into Umbria. Check in to Il Monastero Collection — a converted monastery in the Umbrian hills. Explore the grounds, rest, eat well.
fun_fact: Umbria is called the 'green heart of Italy' — the only landlocked region in central Italy. No coast, no motorway crowds, just medieval hilltowns, truffles and silence.

title: Day 9 — Umbrian Hills 🌄
description: A slower day based at Il Monastero. Walk the surrounding countryside. Visit a nearby hilltown — Spello or Bevagna. Black truffle pasta for dinner, because you have to.
fun_fact: Umbria produces some of Italy's finest black truffles, found under oak trees by trained dogs. A single kilogram can fetch €3,000. The best ones smell of earth, garlic and something ancient.

title: Day 10 — Assisi 🙏
description: Check in to Hotel Assisi. Walk up to the Basilica di San Francesco — one of the most beautiful churches in Italy. The lower basilica is cooler and darker, with Giotto's frescoes. The town is tiny; you can walk everything.
fun_fact: St Francis gave up a life of wealth and military ambition after a series of visions in his early twenties. He founded an order of 5,000 friars before he died at 44. The Basilica began construction within two years of his death.

title: Day 11 — Fattoria Fibbiano 🍷
description: Drive west into Tuscany. Hotel Fattoria Fibbiano is a working winery in the Pisan hills — vineyards, olive groves, terracotta. Wine tasting this evening is not optional.
fun_fact: Tuscany has 11 DOCG wine designations — the highest Italian wine quality tier. The Pisan hills produce Montescudaio wines that most tourists never encounter because they barely leave the region.

title: Day 12 — Tuscan Countryside 🌻
description: Based at Fattoria Fibbiano. Drive into Volterra — an Etruscan city so old it predates Rome. Dramatic clifftop position, alabaster workshops, Roman theatre still visible below the town.
fun_fact: Volterra was a major Etruscan city when Rome was still a village. The Etruscans built here around 800 BC. Their civilisation was eventually absorbed by Rome — but they gave the Romans their alphabet, arch construction, and religious practices.

title: Day 13 — Hotel Recostano 🌿
description: Check in to Hotel Recostano Residence — the last stop before home. Settle in. Find the best local restaurant and eat slowly. Tomorrow is the last full day.
fun_fact: The word 'Tuscany' comes from the Etruscan people (Tusci in Latin) who dominated central Italy before Rome. Even the name of the land remembers them.

title: Day 14 — Last Full Day 🌅
description: The last full day. No rushing. Buy good olive oil and a bottle of something excellent. Walk somewhere beautiful. Eat a long dinner. Come back to the room slow.
fun_fact: Italy is the world's largest wine producer and the largest exporter. The average Italian drinks about 40 litres of wine per year. They consider this moderate.

title: Day 15 — Fly Home ✈️
description: Transfer to airport. The flight home. Sit back, close your eyes, and go through every meal, every piazza, every evening. You'll be back.
fun_fact: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the world — 58 and counting. You've seen some of the best of them.
